rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or Evaluator feedback yet, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Geometry: five sensors spaced 12 mm apart across x = -0.024 to +0.024 m, placed 0.04 m ahead of the axle so steering reacts before the wheels reach the line. The 12 mm sensor footprint is about half the tape width, which gives a usable gradient across the tape. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give a moderate turn authority. Mass 0.8 kg and body 0.16 x 0.12 m are mid-range. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which is 0.06 m for this body, so the body width does not change the limit here. Controller: sensor_weights are proportional to sensor x (left positive, so a left-side sensor reading tape steers the robot left). kp = 2.5 gives a moderate proportional response, kd = 0.3 damps oscillation, and ki = 0.05 is small to avoid integral windup. base_speed = 1.5 is chosen to reach the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s without a large speed margin that would risk leaving the track on the tightest bends. line_loss = last_direction so the robot searches toward the side it last saw the line. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with some oscillation on the slalom. Hypotheses to test: (1) kp is high enough to track bends but kd suppresses jitter; (2) 1.5 m/s is achievable without line loss. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion time, RMS and max error, line-loss events and steering oscillation, which together show whether speed or gain is the limiting factor.
